descriptionChirho: Causal conjunction introducing the reason or ground for a preceding statement, meaning 'since,' 'because,' or 'inasmuch as.' Multilingual evidence uniformly supports the causal reading: spa puesto que, arb بِما أَنَّ (bima anna, 'inasmuch as') / إِذْ (idh, 'since'), kor 왜냐하면 (waenyahamyeon, 'because'), swa kwa kuwa / kwa sababu ('because'), hin क्योंकि (kyonki, 'because'). All 9 occurrences share the same logical-causal function across different syntactic positions.

Temporal conjunction indicating a point in time after which something occurs, meaning 'when' or 'after.' Multilingual evidence clearly distinguishes this from the causal sense: spa después que ('after'), arb بَعدَما (ba'dama, 'after'), kor ~후에 (hu-e, 'after'), swa baada ya ('after'), hin जब (jab, 'when'). This single occurrence (Heb 11:22 or similar context) shows the temporal-sequential rather than logical-causal function of the conjunction.
